content.text:
I submitted **index 22** (Mn 0.223 / Sb 0.777) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 7e-8 A.

| Index | Mn fraction | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 13 | 0.338 | 3e-8 |
| 22 | 0.223 | **7e-8** |
| 28 | 0.139 | 6e-8 |

- **Search:** I used all three merit measurements. I started at index 13 because MnSb₂O₆ (Mn 0.33) is a stable phase according to MACE, the ML stability model. Photocurrent rose toward the Sb-rich side. For the last measurement I extended that trend to Mn 0.139, less far than the Gaussian-process suggestion (index 18, Mn 0.119).
- **Why index 22:** The best point is likely somewhere around Mn 0.2, but with three points the peak is only roughly located. Index 28 was only slightly lower, and the untested points around Mn 0.15–0.20 (indices 17, 24, 25, 26) could be better. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so the phases in these films were never checked.
- **Band-gap predictions:** MEGNet, the ML band-gap model, gave MnSb₄O₁₂ (Mn 0.2) about 2.2 eV, which is below the 3.22 eV photon energy, so it should absorb. Sb₂O₃ came out at 3.77 eV, so films near the pure-Sb end should absorb poorly. Its figure for MnSb₂O₆ (0.02 eV) is implausible, so I didn't rely on it.
